person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts at a chain pharmacy. She came to the US at 19, reads English slowly for official letters, and switches her phone to Vietnamese when she is tired. She has a health FSA and a dependent care FSA through work. The plan year ended on 30 June and she has heard the money can still be claimed until the end of October. Her daughter is 18 and starting college, her son Minh is 9, and her mother lives with them. She manages the family's benefit accounts on her phone, is wary of fees and of helpers who charge, and wants to be sure before anything is sent.
stated_up_front: Hello. I have FSA money from work and I think the time is almost finished. Can you help me ask for my money back for the medical and Minh's camp? Does it cost anything?

facts.about: Plan year and last day to claim
facts.truth: The plan year ended 30 June 2026. The last day to send claims is 31 October 2026.
The Blue Cross explanation of benefits says she owes 142.00 dollars for the crown, done on 12 March 2026.
The explanation of benefits says she owes 60.00 dollars for the visit on 21 April 2026.
Allergy medicine 18.49 dollars on 9 May 2026, and menstrual products 14.25 dollars on 2 June 2026, both paid with her own debit card at CVS.
Minh is 9. The day camp in June cost 280.00 dollars, and the invoice came in the mail.
After-school care for Minh in May cost 120.00 dollars, shown on the center's invoice.
A swipe of 72.30 dollars at a clinic on 18 May 2026 is pending in Flexwell. The deadline on the notice is 27 October 2026.

facts.about: Things she paid for that are not medical
facts.truth: Her bank shows teeth whitening for 89.00 dollars, a gym membership of 25.00 dollars a month, and vitamins for 24.99 dollars at CVS. She does not know if they count.

facts.about: Camp her daughter and son might go to
facts.truth: Minh went to an overnight camp for 350.00 dollars in July 2026, paid in June. It is not day camp.
Minh's orthodontist visit of 30 January 2026 was paid with the FSA card, so she should not ask for it again.

unknowns: Whether the plan accepts her explanation of benefits as proof for the 72.30 dollar swipe, or wants something else
Whether an expense paid in one month but for care in another month counts
Whether her mother, who lives with her, counts as someone she can claim for
What a premium or 'substantiate' means in the plan's rules
